title: Air-Operated Double Diaphragm Pump

introduction.definition: An air-operated double-diaphragm (AODD) pump uses compressed air to push two diaphragms connected by a shaft. While one diaphragm discharges liquid, the other draws liquid in; an air valve shifts the air at each stroke end, and check balls make the flow one-way. It can run dry, self-primes and stalls safely against a closed valve.
key_points: Discharge pressure cannot exceed the air pressure (1:1 models)
Air consumption makes it less energy-efficient

classification.configuration: Double diaphragm, pneumatically driven, mechanically connected diaphragms
classification.valves: Ball check valves (flap valves are an alternative for large solids)

introduction.summary: Compressed air, switched by an air valve, alternately pressurises the air side of two flexible diaphragms joined by a shaft. The pressurised diaphragm pushes liquid out of its chamber through the upper (outlet) ball check, while the other diaphragm is pulled inward, drawing liquid in through its lower (inlet) ball check. At the end of each stroke a pilot shifts the air valve and the cycle reverses. Discharge pressure cannot exceed air supply pressure (1:1 ratio pumps), so the pump simply stalls against a closed valve.

what_to_look_for: Compressed air enters the chamber behind one diaphragm, pushing it outward and discharging liquid.
The shaft pulls the other diaphragm inward, drawing liquid through its inlet ball valve.
At the end of the stroke the pilot valve shifts the air spool, reversing the air flow.

steps.text: Compressed air enters the chamber behind one diaphragm, pushing it outward and discharging liquid.
The shaft pulls the other diaphragm inward, drawing liquid through its inlet ball valve.
At the end of the stroke the pilot valve shifts the air spool, reversing the air flow.
Check balls in the manifolds open and close to keep the flow one-way.
Exhaust air leaves through the muffler.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flow falls as discharge pressure rises; at a given air pressure the pump stalls when discharge pressure equals air pressure.

components.key_components: Two diaphragms, air distribution valve, check balls

parts.name: Centre Section (Air Chamber Block)
parts.function: Separates the two air chambers, guides the shaft and pilot, and carries the air valve and muffler.
parts.material: Aluminium, polypropylene, acetal or conductive polymers; not wetted by the pumped liquid unless a diaphragm fails.

parts.name: Shaft Bushing
parts.function: Guides the diaphragm shaft and limits air leakage between the two air chambers.

parts.name: Air Valve Body
parts.function: Directs supply air to one air chamber while venting the other to exhaust; reverses at each stroke end.

parts.name: Air Valve Spool
parts.function: Moves between two positions to switch the air path.

parts.name: Pilot Shaft (Pilot Valve)
parts.function: Senses end of stroke (contacted by the inner diaphragm plates) and sends pilot air to shift the main air valve.

parts.name: Exhaust Muffler
parts.function: Reduces exhaust noise.

parts.name: Diaphragm Shaft (Connecting Rod)
parts.function: Connects the two diaphragms so one discharges while the other fills.

parts.name: Inner Diaphragm Plate – Left
parts.function: Supports the diaphragm on the air side and contacts the pilot at stroke end.

parts.name: Outer Diaphragm Plate & Nut – Left
parts.function: Clamps the diaphragm centre on the liquid side.

parts.name: Diaphragm – Left
parts.function: Flexible membrane that separates air from liquid and displaces liquid as it moves.
parts.material: Neoprene, Buna-N (NBR), EPDM, Viton (FKM), thermoplastic elastomers (e.g. Santoprene), PTFE; choose by chemical compatibility, temperature and abrasion.

parts.name: Liquid Chamber – Left
parts.function: Contains the liquid on the outside of each diaphragm and carries the check-valve ports.
parts.material: Aluminium, cast iron, stainless steel, polypropylene, PVDF, conductive acetal.

parts.name: Valve Seat – Inlet, Left
parts.function: Sealing surface for the check ball.

parts.name: Check Ball – Inlet, Left
parts.function: One-way valve: lifts to admit or discharge liquid, seats to block back-flow.
parts.material: PTFE, Neoprene, Buna-N, EPDM, Viton, stainless steel; weighted balls for viscous duties.

parts.name: Valve Seat – Outlet, Left
parts.function: Sealing surface for the check ball.

foundation: Free-standing or bolted; vibration isolation pads.
piping: Flexible connections reduce vibration; pulsation dampener on discharge.
Air supply with filter–regulator; air shut-off valve.
commissioning: Start with low air pressure; increase gradually.
Ground the pump for flammable liquids.

lubrication: Most modern air valves are lube-free.

script.narration: This module introduces the Air-Operated Double Diaphragm Pump.
An air-operated double-diaphragm (AODD) pump uses compressed air to push two diaphragms connected by a shaft.
While one diaphragm discharges liquid, the other draws liquid in; an air valve shifts the air at each stroke end, and check balls make the flow one-way.
It can run dry, self-primes and stalls safely against a closed valve.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Air-Operated Double Diaphragm Pump.
Check for leakage at the muffler (diaphragm failure sign).
Replace diaphragms.
Inspect balls and seats.
Rebuild the air valve.
Watch for diaphragm rupture: product out of the exhaust. Common cause: fatigue, chemical attack.
Watch for air valve stalling / icing: pump stops. Common cause: wet air, high air pressure drop.
Watch for check-ball wear: low flow. Common cause: abrasives.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
